calibration_policy: Measure only effective backend service/bandwidth/boundary/overlap parameters whose uncertainty can change the construction; do not treat sample extrema as guaranteed bounds.
conclusion: Prefer source/effect proofs, analytical demand/bounds, structure-specific construction, resource-calendar schedule, and independent certificates; target runs validate predictions, not enumerate versions.

proposed_layers.output: Version/effect/alias/iteration-preserving rewrite and region coverage witnesses
Arithmetic counts, access relations, mandatory movement, live footprint and scoped model lower bounds
Grouping, serial/parallel grain, legal placement, residency, chunk/buffer size from bounds and component cost curves
Dependency-ready task placement into CPU/GPU/link/memory calendars, preserving structured loops
Semantic legality, feasibility, scope/domain/assumptions, lower bound and feasible model cost; optimum only when matching
Existing C++20/ABI1 backend with checked boundary/conditional borrowed core and original fallback, then periodic clean A/B

sources.lesson: Separation of source program and data-centric optimization; nested states/dataflow and symbolic movement.
sources.limits: A representation and transformation framework, not a universal no-search optimizer.
sources.title: DaCe/SDFG

sources.lesson: Bounds analysis, grouping and tiling based on modeled arithmetic/load/recomputation costs.
sources.limits: Greedy grouping and finite tile choices remain; no target autotuning does not imply no search or global optimality.
sources.title: Halide analytic autoscheduling

sources.lesson: Tile/fuse tensors before choosing buffers; analyze aliases and read-after-write conflicts.
sources.limits: One-Shot Bufferize is greedy; not a global memory/time optimizer.
sources.title: MLIR Bufferization

sources.lesson: Graph dependencies and fast-memory capacity constrain required input/output movement.
sources.limits: Must state graph, initial/final locations, recomputation policy and memory capacity; not arbitrary-program closed form.
sources.title: Hong-Kung red-blue pebble

sources.lesson: Relates attainable arithmetic rate to peak compute and sustained memory traffic.
sources.limits: Source loads/stores are not DRAM traffic; empirically calibrated bandwidth is not an unconditional physical bound.
sources.title: Roofline

sources.lesson: Decompose execution and cache/memory transfer costs with explicit overlap assumptions.
sources.limits: Target-specific architectural rules, not a universal CPU/GPU overlap model; caches need not become controllable allocations.
sources.title: Execution-Cache-Memory

sources.lesson: For ideal homogeneous processors, work/span provide max(W/P,S) and a greedy bound W/P+S.
sources.limits: No scheduling, communication or heterogeneous-device costs in this ideal result.
sources.title: Graham-Brent work/span as presented by Blumofe

sources.lesson: Prioritize critical-path ranks and insert tasks into earliest available device slots.
sources.limits: Heuristic, no general global-optimum proof; original communication assumptions omit shared-link contention.
sources.title: HEFT/CPOP

sources.lesson: Construct loop transformations from affine domains/dependencies, then generate code.
sources.limits: Uses integer linear optimization; non-affine references/control require conservative dependencies.
sources.title: Pluto

sources.lesson: Learns cost features and uses beam search, optionally with target autotuning.
sources.limits: Not the proposed default constructive route; does not guarantee a global optimum even with ideal costs.
sources.title: Halide learned autoscheduling
